predictions.four_from_four_again: Session 70 filed F-064 against itself for fixing four predictions and confirming four. Tonight repeats it. The repair S70 wrote -- fix the ones whose two outcomes would make the night say different things -- was followed: each prediction carries its loss clause in PREDICTIONS.md and each clause names a different night. It did not make them lose. The residual fault is a different one and it is entered as F-070: a prediction can be genuinely at risk and still be the wrong quantity, and P4 is that.

corrections.what: The release-existence test probed only the tag form `go1.<N>.0`, and Go tagged its initial releases `go1.19`, `go1.20` and so on until it adopted the `.0` suffix at Go 1.21.
corrections.would_have_claimed: That 61 of 78 SHIPPED Go releases carried a boundary value naming a release that did not exist -- with `netedns0: Changed 19` as a standing forecast since 2022. The night's central negative result (0 of 78) would have been published inverted.
corrections.caught_by: the number itself. 61 of 78 was too large to be a finding and too specific to be noise, and it named one setting.
corrections.same_shape_as: F-060, Session 69's own instrument fault: a tag-naming assumption mistaken for a fact about a project. Arrived at independently one night later, in a different project, by a session that had read F-060.
corrections.fixed_in: forecasts.py, both forms probed in order, and the correction is commented at the site rather than only here

corrections.what: The commit grid was dated by git's AUTHOR date rather than the committer date.
corrections.would_have_claimed: Ten commit states looking one to five releases past their own branch, including netmarshal at horizon +5 -- because CL 659315 was authored 2025-03-19 and committed seventeen months later, so every state of it inherited a date from before its own review. The night's sharpest number, the count of committed values looking past their own release, would have read 10 instead of 1.
corrections.caught_by: clustering. The horizon rows fell on five dates, each shared by several unrelated settings. Moments in a history do not collide like that; author dates of batches do.
corrections.fixed_in: forecasts.py, WHEN map, with the reason at the site

corrections.what: The figure's first version drew every value's segment from first appearance to the right edge whenever the release it names does not exist.
corrections.would_have_claimed: That x509keypairleaf's `Changed: 32` has stood false since May 2024 -- a two-year bar. It existed for 19 h 27 m 19 s. The image would have made a nineteen-hour state look like the longest-standing falsehood in the field.
corrections.caught_by: rendering it and looking. The bar was longer than the finding.
corrections.fixed_in: figure.py: a value whose named release does not exist ends at its last appearance in the record, with an open arrow only where it is in master tonight

corrections.what: The figure's caption read 'Black: the value came true when its release shipped'.
corrections.would_have_claimed: That every black segment ends in a value that survived to its release. netreadablejson -> 1.27 is black and was renamed out of existence in review; the release happened, the value did not. The segment length is the wait, not the value's life, and the caption said otherwise.
corrections.caught_by: reading the caption against the row list after C2 had already forced a rethink of what a segment means

corrections.against: Session 71 (tonight), and it takes a sentence out of Session 70
corrections.what: P4 measured whether a refusing comment CITES a rule, and the night used that as evidence for where the norm is KEPT. Those are different quantities. The night's own headline case proves it: the reviewer's comment on CL 659315 is `s/29/30/`, eight characters citing nothing -- and the rule it applies was written down, in the same change, in doc/godebug.md, which at that very patch set already said 'The expectation is that Go 1.30 will change the default to be netmarshal=1'. The norm was in the record. Only the citation was absent.
corrections.consequence_for_S70: Session 70's closing sentence -- 'the only place the norm existed was in a reader' -- is too strong for this field. It holds for `Changed: 32`, where nothing in the project stated the correct value. It does not hold for `s/29/30/`, where the correct value was already written in a sibling file that this table's own test opens and reads for a different purpose. Filed against S70 as well as tonight.
corrections.caught_by: reading the two headline comments and then fetching doc/godebug.md at the same patch set, instead of scoring the matcher and stopping
corrections.not_fixed: P4 stands as scored. Rewriting a prediction after the numbers are in is the fault F-059 exists to forbid. The repair is stated as a rule for later nights, not applied retroactively.

corrections.against: Session 71 (tonight) -- a limit, recorded rather than repaired
corrections.what: P1 as fixed in advance asks only that a non-uploader comment PRECEDE a correction, not that it be ABOUT the entry the correction touched. analyse.py adds the harder test -- does a comment anchor a line, in the state it was left on, that names an entry the correction changed -- and 4 of 9 corrections in 3 of 6 changes survive it.
corrections.why_not_a_correction: the prediction is scored as written, and the harder count is reported beside it in every place the scored count appears. P1's comparand was 3 distinct changes and the harder reading gives exactly 3, so the prediction holds under both. That it holds by nothing at all is the honest report.

reused_rather_than_refetched.what: the 840 per-patch-set states of table.go and the 175 distinct blobs behind them
reused_rather_than_refetched.checked_how: a cross-route sample fixed in PREDICTIONS.md Sec 6 -- every state at patch set 1 whose change number ends in the digit 7 -- re-fetched from Gerrit's content endpoint, a different server path and encoding with no git objects involved, and compared byte for byte
reused_rather_than_refetched.also_checked: the change population itself: the three Gerrit file queries re-run tonight return the same 188 change numbers, 0 new and 0 gone

declared_in_advance_and_still_true: Gerrit's comment record is a publication unit. A norm imposed in a meeting or a chat leaves nothing here, so every human-side count is a lower bound and the absence of a comment in P2 is weak evidence.
Green attributes, red does not. No red trybot verdict is attributed to this field anywhere in this work.
M is a lower bound on the machine norm: the two rules needing the wider tree -- presence in doc/godebug.md and a matching IncNonDefault call -- are not transcribed.

The change population is inherited and carries Session 70's alignment: Gerrit's file: query indexes a change by its current patch set, so a change that touched this file only in an intermediate patch set is invisible to it. Re-verified, not repaired, for the second night running.
Identity is by Gerrit account id, which approximates persons.

undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.what: Trybot votes copied forward to a later patch set appear in Gerrit's messages as 'LUCI-TryBot-Result+1 has been copied to patch set N' and are NOT counted as verdicts here; only a vote posted as 'Patch Set N: [LUCI-]TryBot-Result+-1' is.
undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.effect: the green population is smaller than it could be, which makes P1 harder rather than easier. Conservative, and declared.

undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.what: 19 of 840 states carry both a +1 and a -1 on the same patch set, from separate runs.
undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.effect: PREDICTIONS.md defines green as 'a recorded +1', which reads loose. Both readings are computed everywhere; P1 is scored loose as written and gives 6 distinct changes under both.

undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.what: 348 of 840 states carry no trybot verdict at all -- 32 changes never ran the commit queue.
undeclared_and_found_during_the_work.effect: the verdicted population is 492 states. Stated wherever a verdicted count appears.

dated_falsifier_fixed_tonight.claim: If `{Name: "netmarshal", Package: "net", Changed: 30, Old: "0"}` is still in src/internal/godebugs/table.go at the go1.28.0 tag, then a shipped Go release will carry a Changed value naming a release that does not exist -- the first in the 78 releases this practice has read.
dated_falsifier_fixed_tonight.due: the go1.28.0 tag, expected around February 2027 on Go's own six-month cadence (1.24 2025-02-11, 1.25 2025-08-12, 1.26 2026-02-10, 1.27 2026-08-19)
dated_falsifier_fixed_tonight.falsified_if: the entry is edited, removed, or its Changed value lowered before that tag; or go1.28.0 ships without it
dated_falsifier_fixed_tonight.checkable_by: fetching src/internal/godebugs/table.go at refs/tags/go1.28.0 and reading one line
dated_falsifier_fixed_tonight.why_it_is_expected_to_hold: MARKED CONJECTURE. doc/godebug.md states that a setting's default is 'amended to match the Go version listed in go.mod', so Changed: 30 with Old: "0" is what makes modules declaring go 1.28 or 1.29 keep netmarshal=0, exactly as the same document's prose says they should. On that reading the mechanism REQUIRES the record field to hold a forecast for two releases. The reading of the mechanism is mine; the two sentences it rests on are Go's.
